definitions.explanation: The unit of electric current, written A.

examples.japanese: ⟦{十|じゅう}→十：00708_juu⟧アンペア⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電流|でんりゅう}→電流：21016_denryuu⟧。
⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三十|さんじゅう}→三十：00984_sanjuu⟧アンペアです。
examples.english: Our home electricity contract is for thirty amps.

examples.japanese: アンペア⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦エアコン→エアコン：05282_eakon⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{電子|でんし}レンジ→電子レンジ：04973_denshirenji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{同時|どうじ}→同時：01592_douji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧とき⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ブレーカー→ブレーカー：07496_bureekaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧。
examples.english: If your amperage is low, the breaker trips when you run the air conditioner and the microwave at the same time.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
In much of Japan a household's electricity contract is set in amperes (30A, 40A, 50A), and the basic charge rises with it. Using more current than the contract allows trips the main breaker (⟦ブレーカー→ブレーカー：07496_bureekaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧), so families on a small contract learn which appliances not to run together.
